This page lists the IAM roles and permissions for Compute Engine. To search through all roles and permissions, see the [role and permission index](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions) .

<td><h4 id="compute.admin" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Admin" tabindex="-1">Compute Admin</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.admin</code> )</p>
<p>Full control of all Compute Engine resources.</p>
<p>If the user will be managing virtual machine instances that are configured to run as a service account, you must also grant the <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/iam.serviceAccountUser</code> role.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Disk</li>
<li>Image</li>
<li>Instance</li>
<li>Instance template</li>
<li>Node group</li>
<li>Node template</li>
<li>Snapshot</li>
</ul></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td><h4 id="compute.instanceAdmin" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Instance Admin (beta)" tabindex="-1">Compute Instance Admin (beta)</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.instanceAdmin</code> )</p>
<p>Permissions to create, modify, and delete virtual machine instances. This includes permissions to create, modify, and delete disks, and also to configure <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/shielded-vm/docs">Shielded VM</a> settings.</p>
<p>If the user will be managing virtual machine instances that are configured to run as a service account, you must also grant the <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/iam.serviceAccountUser</code> role.</p>
<p>For example, if your company has someone who manages groups of virtual machine instances but does not manage network or security settings and does not manage instances that run as service accounts, you can grant this role on the organization, folder, or project that contains the instances, or you can grant it on individual instances.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Disk</li>
<li>Image</li>
<li>Instance</li>
<li>Instance template</li>
<li>Snapshot</li>
</ul></td>

<td><h4 id="compute.instanceAdmin.v1" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Instance Admin (v1)" tabindex="-1">Compute Instance Admin (v1)</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.instanceAdmin.v1</code> )</p>
<p>Full control of Compute Engine instances, instance groups, disks, snapshots, and images. Read access to all Compute Engine networking resources.</p>
<p>If you grant a user this role only at an instance level, then that user cannot create new instances.</p></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td><h4 id="compute.loadBalancerAdmin" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Load Balancer Admin" tabindex="-1">Compute Load Balancer Admin</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.loadBalancerAdmin</code> )</p>
<p>Permissions to create, modify, and delete load balancers and associate resources.</p>
<p>For example, if your company has a load balancing team that manages load balancers, SSL certificates for load balancers, SSL policies, and other load balancing resources, and a separate networking team that manages the rest of the networking resources, then grant this role to the load balancing team's group.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Instance</li>
</ul></td>

<tr class="even">
<td><h4 id="compute.networkAdmin" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Network Admin" tabindex="-1">Compute Network Admin</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.networkAdmin</code> )</p>
<p>Permissions to create, modify, and delete networking resources, except for firewall rules and SSL certificates. The network admin role allows read-only access to firewall rules, SSL certificates, and instances (to view their ephemeral IP addresses). The network admin role does not allow a user to create, start, stop, or delete instances.</p>
<p>For example, if your company has a security team that manages firewalls and SSL certificates and a networking team that manages the rest of the networking resources, then grant this role to the networking team's group. Or, if you have a combined team that manages both security and networking, then grant this role as well as the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/compute#compute.securityAdmin"><code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/compute.securityAdmin</code></a> role to the combined team's group.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Instance</li>
</ul></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td><h4 id="compute.networkUser" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Network User" tabindex="-1">Compute Network User</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.networkUser</code> )</p>
<p>Provides access to a shared VPC network</p>
<p>Once granted, service owners can use VPC networks and subnets that belong to the host project. For example, a network user can create a VM instance that belongs to a host project network but they cannot delete or create new networks in the host project.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Subnetwork</li>
</ul></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td><h4 id="compute.viewer" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Viewer" tabindex="-1">Compute Viewer</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.viewer</code> )</p>
<p>Read-only access to get and list Compute Engine resources, without being able to read the data stored on them.</p>
<p>For example, an account with this role could inventory all of the disks in a project, but it could not read any of the data on those disks.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Disk</li>
<li>Image</li>
<li>Instance</li>
<li>Instance template</li>
<li>Node group</li>
<li>Node template</li>
<li>Snapshot</li>
</ul></td>

<td><h4 id="compute.xpnAdmin" class="role-title add-link" data-text="Compute Shared VPC Admin" tabindex="-1">Compute Shared VPC Admin</h4>
<p>( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/  compute.xpnAdmin</code> )</p>
<p>Permissions to administer <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/shared-vpc">shared VPC</a> host projects, specifically enabling the host projects and associating shared VPC service projects to the host project's network.</p>
<p>At the organization level, this role can only be granted by an organization admin.</p>
<p>Google Cloud recommends that the Shared VPC Admin be the owner of the shared VPC host project. The Shared VPC Admin is responsible for granting the Compute Network User role ( <code dir="ltr" translate="no">roles/compute.networkUser</code> ) to service owners, and the shared VPC host project owner controls the project itself. Managing the project is easier if a single principal (individual or group) can fulfill both roles.</p>
<p>Lowest-level resources where you can grant this role:</p>
<ul>
<li>Folder</li>
</ul></td>
